questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to my choice of destination, that there would be a mixture of good social opportunities and academic opportunities, where I could at the same time explore new cultural aspects first hand. Edinburgh was the perfect balance, where I had heard of other peoples' good experiences both with the university's social life and the city and area surrounding it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find most information. The only thing to look out for is that there is a lot of information to check out beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: After arriving at the destination the university was very helpful, as one could show up at their office and gain assistance in anything from questions about the studies to changing courses etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find off campus housing. There is currently a lack of housing in Edinburgh and the university does not guarantee housing for exchange students currently. I was lucky enough to get university-run accommodation, however this was only after calling the office over 20 times, as they in practice did not automatically offer student accommodation to any exchange students. It was rather a first-come-first-serve basis that applied, where it was whoever called the office first after a room was emptied that would get the offer.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It should be noted that it is generally no issue to live off campus in Edinburgh, as it is a very friendly city for walking and public transport in general. So do not worry if you find accommodation outside of the centre. You can also find private accommodation and there is a lot of references to pages on the University of Edinburgh's own website.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was mostly straight forward, the only exception being that not all processes that we were asked to do was required for exchange students. This included English proficiency tests under certain circumstances.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was in general a lot of information available on both KU's and Edinburgh's university page, and you could probably also call the University of Edinburgh's offices during their opening hours to get further assistance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not very successful in getting the classes that I actually wanted, as it was given on a first-come-first-serve basis, and there was only 1-5 free spots per course by the time we as exchange students were offered any subjects. I therefore ended up with my 14th and 15th priority for example, but this turned out to be a positive surprise in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to not stress too much about which subjects you end up with initially. This is because you can change courses up to a month into the semester according to the guidelines when I was there. I could therefore change the subjects which I did not want. I also know many others who changed courses to have more 1st-year courses as they were seemingly easier than 3rd- and 4th-year courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses vary a lot, as some courses can be viewed as easier, whereas others can seem very burdening in contrast. There is not any absolute rule to the difference of level of the courses, other than the general trend of 1st-year courses being easier than later courses most often.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You have to be prepared for the teaching style to be quite different, as the courses are often either exclusively seminar-based or a mix of lectures and tutorials, which are shorter meetings in small groups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all the following courses that I was enrolled in:
LAWS10252 - Street Law: public legal education in the community
LAWS10262 - International Human Rights in the Digital Era
LAWS08114 - International Law Ordinary (semester 1)

I would recommend these cases as they were of differing work loads, and gave a broad insight into different fields of law, and offered very different teaching styles.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There was not really any unexpected costs experienced, however it should be noted that costs add up and many small visits can suddenly have quite a cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was in general more expensive than expected, as you need to know the right places to eat at, as the base-cost of most places are very similar, and only few places offer similar experiences at much lower prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a plethora of sports and various social groups, like film and hot chocolate groups, to participate in, which I know many students were happy with. It can be a bit more difficult to interact with these as exchange students given that less people want to interact much with people they know will be gone just three months later or so.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to participate in any that you find interresting. It is mostly just about going in with an open mind, and then you will meet nice people and have plenty of fun for sure.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definately recommend to read through the long list of student societies, as there are so many that you can find social groups no matter what your interests or hobbies are.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to adjust culturally to being in Edinburgh. The only thing that could be challenging to some, is that the food is very different to what we are used to in Denmark. However, this shouldn't be a big issue at all, and you may even find new habits in the city that you don't have at home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be recommended to be in a university-led accommodation, as you can meet many students this way even if you don't participate much in the student led societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The one I personally found most challenging was to adapt to the food available, however this was no major issue.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I most appreciated the social aspects of the culture as people were in general very friendly and helpful. There was furthermore also always opportunities for a good party with friends, where you could also meet new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The most important things I would say would be ahead of time with looking for accommodation, both private and university accommodation, as this will reduce stress ahead of your arrival, I would also recommend to do join as many social activities and societies as you can, so you can figure out which ones you like and in general meet many new people. Last I would recommend not to worry too much about which subjects to get initially as these can be changed later, as spots become available as other students change subjects and as you figure out what you actually like. And in general - be open minded!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would also recommend to have some extra savings when you go to Edinburgh, as there are many opportunities to travel around in Scotland and the broader UK. Having a good budget for travels to cities and nature can only be highly recommended.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the experience was to go to somewhere completely new and meet many new people and face the challenges of studying abroad in a new state and culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There wasn't many big challenges, but the largest one was probably the balance between not falling behind on studies, whilst trying to keep up with as many social activities as possible, as lots were available.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
